Layout notes

    How the VeeTable system fits together
    • 64 mm Vee grid. Every Vee is 90°, 4 mm deep and 8 mm wide at the surface. Bins sit on whole 64 mm cells.
    • 96 mm dog holes. 96 mm is 1.5 cells, so holes alternate between a Vee line and a cell centre. The two patterns line up every 192 mm.
    • Centred holes. A cell count divisible by 3 (6, 9, 12, 18…) can't centre the most holes, so one side ends up half a cell further in. Go one cell up or down, or choose "Always centred".
    • Holes stay inside the frame. No hole centre is closer than 32 mm to the outer Vee.
    • Cut order. Drill the dog holes and fixing holes first, then cut the Vees.
    Bin generator

    Storage bins that lock into your VeeTable

    Design your own bins on MakerWorld and print them at home. They drop into the 64 mm Vee grid and stay put while you slide timber and tools across the bench. When you need one, lift it straight out.

    What you can make

    • Any size from 1 × 1 to 6 × 6 grid units (64 to 384 mm), any depth from 15 mm
    • Stacking rim so bins stack and lock on each other
    • Matching lids that locate on the bin and stack too
    • Dividers along and across, spaced how you like
    • Scoops on the front, or in every compartment
    • ¼″ hex bit holders, a whole bin, or a section in one side or corner
    • Text labels, engraved or raised, on the front, the label shelf or the lid
    • Prints without supports, with 3 mm walls and soft rounded edges

    Send feedback →
    Exports contain these layers: OUTLINE, V_GROOVES (centrelines for an on-the-line 90° V-bit toolpath, 4 mm deep), V_CORNERS (8 mm squares to V-carve for sharp outer corners), DOG_HOLES (Ø20 mm), FIXINGS (bolt holes) and a FIX_POCKETS layer named with its depth. Files are drawn in the units you choose above, with the origin at the front-left corner. No toolpaths or G-code are included.

    Check before you cut

    • Check every dimension against your own sheet, tools, machine settings and any frame you're fitting the top to.
    • Pay particular attention to hole sizes, fixing positions and how your sheet's thickness suits your frame.
    • Try a test cut on scrap first.

    Work safely

    Routers, drills and CNC machines can cause serious injury. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for every tool, wear suitable eye, ear and dust protection, and clamp your work securely. You are responsible for working safely.

    Stand pockets

    The stand pocket feature is made for one stand size only (2′ × 4′, 6 heads). Stands can differ between models and over time. Set up your own stand and check every head position against the drawing before cutting. If you allow dog holes over the stand heads, dogs or clamps pushed through can hit the stand and move the top.

    VeeTable collects no personal data. There are no accounts, no cookies, no analytics, no tracking and no adverts.

    Everything stays on your device

    Drawings and files are made in your browser. Nothing you type or download is sent to me or anyone else.

    Remembered settings

    So the designer opens where you left it, your last settings are saved in your own browser's local storage. Only your browser can read them; I never see them. You can clear them here at any time.

    Settings cleared.

    Hosting

    The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. Like any web host, GitHub receives your IP address and basic browser details when the page loads, and may keep these in logs for security and to run the service. I don't receive or have access to them. See GitHub's privacy statement.

    No outside services

    The fonts and code are part of this page, so it loads nothing from other companies.

    Links to other sites

    The MakerWorld and feedback buttons open other websites in a new tab, and nothing is sent unless you click them. The feedback form is a Google Form, so Google's privacy policy applies there. It only collects what you type in. Your email address is optional and is used only to reply to you.
